NewYorkPage.title: Build your first AI agent with Microsoft Foundry
NewYorkPage.intro: Follow these steps to set up Microsoft Foundry with your Azure for Students account and create your first AI agent.

portal.title: Go to the Azure for Students portal
portal.body: Sign in with your school account to get your free Azure for Students subscription.

search.title: Search for Foundry
search.body: In the Azure portal search bar, type “foundry” and select Microsoft Foundry.

create.title: Create a resource
create.body: Select Create, or Create a resource.

properties.title: Set the properties
properties.body: Choose the Azure for Students subscription and create a resource group, for example “lead”.

name.title: Name your project
name.body: Give your resource and your first project a name.

review.title: Review and create
review.body: Select Review + create. You’ll see “Deployment in progress”; it takes a couple of minutes.

goToPortal.title: Go to the Foundry portal
goToPortal.body: When the deployment is complete, select Go to Foundry portal.

home.title: Explore the Foundry home
home.body: You land on the Foundry home page. Your API key and project endpoint are here; you’ll need them to connect your app.

playground.title: Test in the playground
playground.body: Back on the Foundry home, select Test in playground and try the sample scenario: a purchase in Dallas followed minutes later by a large charge in another country.

ownAgent.title: Create your own agent!
ownAgent.body: Go to Agents and build your own. Paste these instructions into your agent. If Foundry says you don’t have permission, select Assign me the Foundry User role.

NewYorkPage.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text instead.

gate.title: Unlock the instructions
gate.body: Enter your email to see the step-by-step guide.
gate.label: Email
gate.error: Enter a valid email, like name@school.edu.

LoginPage.title: Sign in
LoginPage.subtitle: Use your Google account to continue.
LoginPage.error: We couldn't sign you in. Try again.

DesignSystemPage.title: LEAD design system
DesignSystemPage.intro: The tokens and components this app uses. Build only from them: don't invent new colors, fonts or radii.

colors.title: Color
colors.semantic: Semantic colors: components use these, and they change between light and dark themes.
colors.identity: Identity colors: the same in both themes, for large fields, graphics and the gradient.

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: Montserrat for headlines, Source Sans 3 for everything else. One display or h1 per page.

samples.body-lg: A network of professionals and students empowering the next generation of Latino leaders.
samples.body: Sign up before March 15 to save your spot.
samples.label: Email
samples.small: We'll send you a confirmation email.
samples.caption: Updated 2 days ago

spacing.title: Spacing
spacing.description: 4px base. In Tailwind, p-5 equals space-5 (24px). Use steps 1 to 8 only.

shape.title: Radius, shadow and gradients
shape.description: radius-xl (30px) is the brand's maximum. The brand gradient appears once per view at most, never in app controls.

components.title: Components
components.description: They live in src/components/ui with the same names and props as the design system.
components.gradientNote: Gradient: marketing and email only, never in the app.
components.emailHelp: We'll send you a confirmation email.
components.name: Name
components.tooltip: Spots are assigned in order of sign-up.

table.caption: AI Budget Games participants
table.name: Name
table.note: Headers in label on surface-alt, cells in small, numbers right-aligned. The selected row uses primary-soft. Status always carries an icon and words.
table.empty: No participants yet. Share the program to start getting sign-ups.
